new_scholarship.description: The France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship Program was developed by the French Ministry of Foreign Affairs to help French higher education institutions attract the best foreign students to Master's and doctoral degree programmes, and to train future decision-makers in the public and private sectors. It covers seven areas of study grouped under Science and Technology and Humanities and Social Sciences. Applications are submitted exclusively by French higher education institutions; applications sent directly by students or by foreign institutions are declared ineligible. The programme funds a monthly allowance plus services such as international and national transportation, insurance, housing searches and cultural activities, but does not cover tuition fees.

new_scholarship.description: Each year the Swiss Confederation awards Government Excellence Scholarships to encourage international exchange and research cooperation between Switzerland and over 180 other countries. Recipients are selected by the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students, also known as ESKAS. The scholarships are mainly intended for talented early career researchers from abroad who have already completed a Master's degree, and the programme is currently open to applicants from 183 countries. Funding is CHF 2450 per month for a maximum period of 12 or 36 months for research scholarships and 21 months for art scholarships, with a maximum age of 35. Applications are open from 20 August 2026 and must be prepared in the GO ESKAS application platform using a Switch edu-ID.

Art scholarship applicants must hold a Bachelor's degree and hold an admission or proof of application, and are eligible from a limited number of countries only. The maximum age is 35.

programme_detail_official.description: Since 2018 the Make Our Planet Great Again initiative has attracted strong interest from the international scientific community and has become a flagship programme for postdoctoral mobility in France and one of the leading fellowship programmes of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. The 2027 call is the tenth edition, funded by MEAE in partnership with MESRE and implemented by Campus France, and enables young international researchers to carry out a research project in France. Fellowships run for 12 months and include exclusively a monthly allowance of EUR 2,500, a EUR 500 settling-in allowance, and health coverage comprising health insurance, civil liability insurance and repatriation assistance followed by supplementary health insurance after French social security registration. Applicants must have defended their PhD between December 2021 and December 2026, hold a nationality other than French, not be residing and professionally active in France, and not have received a MOPGA fellowship before. Projects must fall within five research themes and adopt an integrated One Health approach. Successful applicants receive French Government Scholarship holder status, must sign a research stay agreement with the host institution, and cannot combine the fellowship with a French employment contract or other French government funding. International travel is not covered.

First- and higher-semester students of all nationalities can apply directly to their university. Funding is normally granted for at least two semesters, up to a maximum covering the standard period of study, with a review every two semesters.

research_notes.logo: Scanned the Deutschlandstipendium homepage markup for logo assets. Two candidates: /SiteGlobals/Frontend/Images/icons/_common/bmftr-logo.svg (the ministry logo) and /SiteGlobals/Frontend/Images/icons/deutschlandstipendium/logo-deutschlandstipendium.jpg (the programme's own wordmark). Both were probed, but the first probe of each path returned text/html 81962 B and 82157 B, because the site only serves the raw asset when the __blob=normal parameter is present. Re-probing with the exact URLs taken from the page markup gave HTTP 200 image/svg+xml 27605 B for the ministry logo and HTTP 200 image/jpeg 8530 B for the programme logo. The programme wordmark was rendered on a white card and confirmed as the orange bracket with black 'Deutschland STIPENDIUM' text, dark-on-light and fully visible, so it was selected as the award's own mark on the awarding body's own domain. The stored image was a Mottoschmiede artwork hosted on the third-party domain motte-models.com, a disqualifying third-party asset, and was replaced. Other images on the page, such as the jubilee city motifs and the university teaser photo, are campaign photographs rather than marks and were rejected.
